region: Alto Agrelo · Luján de Cuyo, Mendoza, Argentina
about: Finca Wölffer is the Argentine chapter of the Long Island estate. Co-owner Marc Wölffer cultivates vineyards in Mendoza, and Wölffer’s winemaker and partner Roman Roth has worked there since 2015 with the team at Dominio del Plata, the Luján de Cuyo winery founded by Susana Balbo, which produces and bottles the wine. It brings Wölffer’s house style, built around freshness and balance, to Argentina’s signature grape.

The vines grow in the Alto Agrelo district of Luján de Cuyo, about 4,100 feet up at the foot of the Andes, in sandy loam under an arid, cool climate with more than 300 sunny days a year. Altitude brings cold nights that keep acidity bright while the grapes ripen fully, which is why Mendoza Malbec at this height tends toward fruit and structure rather than heaviness.

Wölffer describes the 2024 as concentrated and fruit-driven, with blueberry, fig and dark berries on the nose, black cherry and dark chocolate on the palate, velvety tannins, chalky minerality and a touch of iodine on the finish. The winery suggests serving it at cellar temperature, around 56°F. It is an approachable, modern Malbec, a fine match for grilled and wood-fired meats.
